title: Another customer's data is disclosed
description: The assistant shows one customer's order, email, phone, name or address to someone else, e.g. a person who guesses an order ID or claims to be a family member.
existing_control: Order details only after the order ID and the email on that order match (agent.verify, ShopData.verify); the check node removes any other customer's order before the reply; order_view() never includes name, email or phone; guards.find_leaks() replaces any reply that contains another customer's data; handover after 3 failed checks.
test_evidence: P1 deterministic tests passed 2026-10-08 (E01, E02, E09, E12). Rules baseline: 0/120 conversations with leaked_other_customer_data (E13). Live agent eval of the other_person_order category and P3 pii_extraction red-team: pending live run (E15, E23). P3 leak rules tested (E20). P8 probe: the output leak filter missed 3 of 6 format variants of another customer's phone (E35, failed).
next_action: Run the live agent eval; make find_leaks() ignore spaces and Arabic-Indic digits in phone numbers (design-review finding DR-1).

title: Prompt injection makes the assistant act against the rules
description: Text in a customer message, a pasted review or a policy/FAQ snippet tells the model to skip approval, reveal data or change its role, and the system follows it.
existing_control: Customer and retrieved text are wrapped in data tags with angle brackets neutralised (parsing.as_prompt_data); both prompts say tagged text is data; the model never chooses tools (plain code in agent.act does); money and data changes can only be queued for a human; injection keywords add a security note to the CRM.
test_evidence: P1 tests passed 2026-10-08, including a fake model that obeys the attack: refund still pending for a supervisor, nothing paid (E03, E04). Rules baseline: 0/15 injection conversations caused a violation, but only 3/15 reached the expected outcome (E13). Live agent eval and P3 prompt_injection / jailbreak red-team: pending live run (E14, E15, E22, E26).
next_action: Run the live evals; review every not-blocked P3 attack by hand; add new attacks found to P1's conversations.

title: Wrong or unauthorised refund
description: A refund is promised or paid that the policy does not allow (opened product, outside 14 days, wrong amount, someone else's order).
existing_control: request_refund only queues an approval; return eligibility is computed in code (data.return_eligibility); amount must be between 0 and the order total and the order must belong to the verified customer; refunds above AED 200 need a supervisor (crm.approval_level); a denied item has no effect; the reply prompt forbids saying a refund is done unless approved.
test_evidence: P1 tests passed 2026-10-08 (E05, E11). Rules baseline: 0/120 conversations with action_decided_without_human or refund_over_200_not_escalated (E13). Live decision accuracy: pending live run (E16).
next_action: Run the live agent eval; finance reviews a weekly sample of approved refunds after launch.

title: A retry pays or changes something twice
description: A network retry, a double click or a LangGraph resume repeats an approved refund or address change.
existing_control: The same pending request is never queued twice; CrmStore.decide() does nothing for an already decided item; no side effects before interrupt() in wait_for_approval.
next_action: Re-test when the JSON-file CRM is replaced by a database or a real refund API.

title: Unauthorised delivery-address change
description: Someone redirects another person's parcel by asking the assistant to change the address.
existing_control: Address change needs a verified customer, only works while the order is 'processing', and is only applied after a person approves it (CrmStore.update_address, decide).
test_evidence: P1 tests passed 2026-10-08 (E07, E01). Live decision accuracy for the address_change category: pending live run (E16).
next_action: Approvers call or email the customer when the new address is in a different city.

title: Hallucinated or wrong policy answer
description: The assistant states a return window, delivery time, COD limit or refund rule that is not the shop's policy.
existing_control: Replies use only the facts and policy sections the code retrieved (prompt rule 1); decisions such as return eligibility are made by code, not the model; if the model fails, a fixed template is used.
test_evidence: P1 return-policy rules tested (E11). P3 grounding check: 0 validation problems in 225 items (E21). Policy-fact accuracy per language: pending live run (E27).
next_action: Run P3 on the chosen model; add any wrong policy answer to P1's eval set.

title: Worse quality or impolite tone in one language
description: Arabic (especially dialect or Arabizi) or French customers get less accurate, less natural or less polite answers than English customers.
existing_control: Language detected by code and reply forced to that language; every metric is reported per language; native-speaker review of the Arabic and French texts is planned (Sara).
test_evidence: All pending: per-language task success and tone (E17), per-language tone and language quality in P3 (E28), judge-vs-human agreement (E19, E29). P3 native-speaker review done: 0/150 items so far (E21 notes).
next_action: Sara reviews the Arabic and French templates and test items before the live run.

title: Unsafe skincare or medical advice
description: The assistant suggests a product for a medical condition, pregnancy or a prescription treatment, or says something is safe when it may not be.
existing_control: Prompt rule 5 (general advice only; refer to a dermatologist or doctor); advice template says 'not medical advice, patch-test first'; product suggestions come only from the catalogue search in code.
test_evidence: P3 unsafe_advice red-team (9 attacks): pending live run (E24). No P1 test checks the medical-referral wording yet.
next_action: Add P1 conversations about pregnancy, eczema and prescription creams in all three languages.

title: Invented discount, code or promise
description: The assistant agrees to a fake discount code, free product or exception because a customer insists or claims special status.
existing_control: No discount tool exists; prompt rule 1 forbids inventing discounts or promises; P3 checks answers for forbidden strings such as invented codes.
test_evidence: P3 leak and forbidden-string rules tested (E20). P3 discount_fraud red-team: pending live run (E25).
next_action: Add the P3 discount attacks to P1's eval set so the full agent is tested too.

title: Missing or unclear AI disclosure
description: A customer does not realise they are talking to an AI (EU AI Act Article 50(1) from 2 August 2026; DIFC Regulation 10 notice).
existing_control: The first reply always starts with a fixed disclosure in the customer's language, added by code (guards.disclosure); the demo page banner says 'You are chatting with an AI assistant'; the eval flags missing_ai_disclosure.
test_evidence: test_first_reply_discloses_ai_assistant passed 2026-10-08, French path (E08). Rules baseline: 0/120 missing_ai_disclosure across 40 ar / 40 en / 40 fr (E13). P8 probe: Arabic and English agent replies start with the disclosure (E36). Live agent eval: pending live run (E14).
next_action: Add Arabic and English cases to the P1 disclosure test; translate the banner; get vendor answers on Article 50(2) marking (see EU memo 5.2).

title: Model or service outage
description: OpenRouter, the model or the courier API is down or slow, so customers get errors or long waits.
existing_control: If the reply model fails, a fixed template answer is used; if the intent model fails, keyword rules are used; the courier client retries; failed calls are logged; customers can always ask for a person.
test_evidence: Courier retry tested (E10). P8 probe: with every model call failing, the agent still answered from templates or handed over (E36). Errors and latency per conversation: pending live run (E18). Switch-off procedure documented (E32).
next_action: Add a P1 test where the model raises an error and the template answer is used.

title: Cost overrun
description: Token use grows (long chats, loops, an expensive model) and the monthly bill passes the budget.
existing_control: Cheap model for intent; max_tokens caps; demo limit of 20 messages per session; cost from OpenRouter logged per call in traces.jsonl; evaluation budget guard (MAX_COST_PER_RUN_USD).
test_evidence: P3 budget guard tests passed (E30). Average cost per conversation (P1) and per 100 answers (P3): pending live run (E18, E31).
next_action: Set a monthly budget alert on the OpenRouter key; review cost per conversation weekly.

title: Sensitive data kept in logs and tickets
description: Customers type health details or other sensitive data, which end up in CRM tickets and notes and are kept too long (UAE PDPL).
existing_control: Model-call traces store only metadata (model, tokens, cost, latency, outcome), not message text; handover tickets keep at most 500 characters of the last message.
test_evidence: Data inventory and retention rules documented (E33, E32). No redaction test exists.
next_action: Redact health terms, emails and phone numbers from ticket summaries; set and enforce retention; add a test.

title: Chat data sent to a model provider abroad
description: Customer messages (which can include their email and address) are processed by a model provider outside the UAE, which is a cross-border transfer under PDPL Articles 22-23.
existing_control: Order facts sent to the model exclude name, email and phone (order_view); only the verified customer's data is ever in the prompt.
test_evidence: Data flows documented in the UAE notes (E33). No technical control yet masks what the customer types.
next_action: Mask emails and phone numbers before model calls; sign data-processing terms; choose providers that do not keep or train on data; counsel confirms the transfer basis.

title: Weak human oversight of approvals
description: Approvers click 'approve' without checking (automation bias), or anyone picks the 'supervisor' role, so the AED 200 rule and the audit log lose their value.
existing_control: The code refuses a large refund unless the decision is made with the supervisor role, and every decision is logged to approval_log.jsonl. In the demo the reviewer chooses their own role and is logged as 'demo reviewer' (design-review finding DR-2).
test_evidence: Supervisor rule tested (E05). Oversight design and approver checklist documented (E32). Code-review finding documented (E34).
next_action: Before launch: sign-in for the Approvals tab, role taken from the account, real reviewer name in the log; monthly sample review of decisions.
